methodology_baseline: Composite IT/OT Industrial Benchmark (Gartner Industrial Cohort, CMMI v2.0, NIST CSF 2.0)

justifications.default: The industry benchmark reflects the empirical median (P50) for heavy process manufacturing and continuous industrial operations. Standardized IT commodity domains (Data Center, Workplace) operate with higher maturity (3.75 - 3.80), while operational technology (OT) and shopfloor plant systems reflect lower structural maturity (3.05 - 3.25) due to long capital depreciation cycles of 20 to 30 years.
justifications.T1: High maturity (3.80) due to widespread consolidation into standardized Tier-III colocation facilities and automated power/thermal management.
justifications.T2: Mature virtualization and hybrid cloud adoption (3.65) supported by enterprise hyperconverged platforms.
justifications.T3: Standardized SD-WAN connectivity and dual-homed telecom access for manufacturing plants (3.65).
justifications.T4: Centralized SAN/NAS storage arrays with structured replication profiles (3.55).
justifications.T5: Constrained shopfloor continuity and OT backup maturity (3.05) driven by legacy PLC lifecycles and heterogeneous plant automation.
justifications.T6: Industrial cybersecurity posture (3.35) undergoing active NIS2 compliance elevation but impacted by legacy IT/OT segmentation challenges.
justifications.T7: Relational database administration and transactional telemetry (3.40) supporting enterprise ERP systems.
justifications.T8: Core ERP governance (3.55) supporting international multi-entity supply chain and financial operations.
justifications.T9: Workplace and collaboration maturity (3.75) underpinned by standardized cloud productivity suites and modern endpoint management.
justifications.T10: Plant dispatch and industrial weighbridge systems (3.25) constrained by localized dependencies and legacy serial communications.
